Use the standard circuit/minimal-dependence representation.

- For the first conjunct, choose \(e\in C\), using that a circuit is nonempty. An element lying in a circuit is not a coloop of \(M\), hence it is not a loop of \(M^\ast\). Thus \(\{e\}\) is independent in the dual, which witnesses `M.dual.RankPos`.

- The left side of the second equivalence is the general support property of the fundamental circuit:
  \[
  \operatorname{fundCircuit}_M(e,I)\subseteq I\cup\{e\}.
  \]
  Discharge it with the library lemma expressing this containment.

- The right side is the usual characterization of a circuit as a minimal dependent set:
  \[
  C\text{ is a circuit}\iff
  C\text{ is dependent and }\forall e\in C,\ C\setminus\{e\}\text{ is independent}.
  \]
  Use the corresponding circuit characterization lemma, or derive the reverse direction by taking a circuit contained in the dependent set \(C\); if it were proper, deleting an element of \(C\) outside that circuit would leave a dependent set, contradicting the assumed independence.

Since both universally quantified statements in the `Iff` are unconditional matroid facts, prove each separately and combine them with `Iff.intro`. The only substantive witness choice is an element of the nonempty circuit in the first conjunct.
